cards.design_implication: If designing a similar timing array study, consider adopting an observational window of approximately 13 years and including multiple observatories to gather TOA data for a comparable number of millisecond pulsars.
does_not_establish: Statistical methods used for timing model fitting
cards.evidence_excerpt: We present time-of-arrival (TOA) measurements and timing models of 47 millisecond pulsars observed from 2004 to 2017 at the Arecibo Observatory and the Green Bank Telescope by the North American Nanohertz Observatory for Gravitational Waves (NANOGrav).
limitations: This claim is derived solely from an abstract and does not provide details on specific instrument settings, data reduction pipelines, or selection criteria for the 47 pulsars.
cards.statement: The study presents time-of-arrival (TOA) measurements and timing models for 47 millisecond pulsars observed from 2004 to 2017 at the Arecibo Observatory and the Green Bank Telescope by NANOGrav.

cards.design_implication: If implementing similar TOA analysis, one might consider a narrowband approach that calculates multiple TOAs within narrow radio-frequency bands using simultaneously collected wide-bandwidth data.
does_not_establish: Specific software packages used for analysis
Error margins of the TOA calculations
cards.evidence_excerpt: We detail our observational methods and present a set of TOA measurements, based on “narrowband” analysis, in which many TOAs are calculated within narrow radio-frequency bands for data collected simultaneously across a wide bandwidth.
limitations: The abstract does not specify the exact width of the narrow radio-frequency bands or the specific algorithms used for TOA calculation.
cards.statement: The TOA measurements are based on narrowband analysis, in which many TOAs are calculated within narrow radio-frequency bands for data collected simultaneously across a wide bandwidth.

cards.design_implication: If replicating this observational strategy, consider maintaining a cadence of 3-4 weeks for the majority of sources, while potentially increasing frequency to weekly for a small subset of priority sources.
does_not_establish: The specific criteria for choosing weekly-observed targets
The total number of observations completed
The impact of cadence on timing residuals
cards.evidence_excerpt: The observing cadence was three to four weeks for most pulsars over most of this time span, with weekly observations of six sources.
limitations: This cadence information is from an abstract and does not explain the rationale for selecting the six weekly-observed sources or account for weather or scheduling interruptions.
cards.statement: The observing cadence was three to four weeks for most pulsars over most of the time span, with weekly observations of six sources.
